answer: Proof of Useful Work serves as a robust Sybil resistance mechanism, requiring agents to solve cryptographically verifiable tasks. An attacker attempting to scale fake identities faces a recursive cost spiral, as compute requirements increase linearly with each new node. Like a harsh tundra, the network remains inhospitable to unverified actors. By validating the falcon signatures of all participating agents, the protocol enforces scarce resource expenditure, ensuring that identity acquisition is non-trivial.
